title: Nondeterministic simulation of an extended word RAM
statement: Let $P$ be an extended word RAM program, and let $W,TW,SW:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be functions such that some finite deterministic Turing machine, on every Boolean input $x$, outputs the $W(|x|)$-bit representation of $W(|x|)$ within $TW(|x|)$ steps and uses exactly $SW(|x|)$ work-tape cells. Then there are a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ and a natural number $A$ such that, for every Boolean input $x$ and all $t,f\in\mathbb{N}$, if for every coin sequence $\rho$ there are a Boolean value and an output string for which $P$ halts on $x$ with word width $W(|x|)$, in fewer than $t$ steps, touching at most $f$ memory addresses, then every length-$s$ choice sequence makes $N$ halt on $x$ within $s=TW(|x|)+A(t+1)(f(W(|x|)+1)+W(|x|)^2+|x|+1)$ steps and use at most $SW(|x|)+A(f(W(|x|)+1)+W(|x|)+\lceil\log_2(|x|+1)\rceil+1)$ work-tape cells. Moreover, $N$ accepts on $x$ within $s$ steps if and only if there exist a coin sequence $\rho$ and an output string $o$ such that $P$ halts with Boolean result true and output $o$ on $x$ with word width $W(|x|)$, in fewer than $t$ steps, touching at most $f$ memory addresses.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is an extended word RAM program
$W,TW,SW$ are functions from natural numbers to natural numbers
$W$ is computable by a finite deterministic Turing machine that outputs its $W(n)$-bit representation within $TW(n)$ steps and uses exactly $SW(n)$ work-tape cells

For every Boolean input $x$, natural numbers $t,f$, and coin sequence $\rho$, there exist a Boolean value and output string witnessing that $P$ halts with word width $W(|x|)$ in fewer than $t$ steps while touching at most $f$ addresses
The simulated Turing machine halts for every choice sequence of the specified length and obeys the stated space bound
